newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Cylinder position rolled forward in BAT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Cylinder position rolled forward in BAT.

text.p: Traded options in B.A.T Industries were busy on Thursday.
The main deal was the rolling forward of a position to protect a shareholding in a collar or cylinder strategy, dealers said.

It involved closing a position in the April 460/500 series ahead of next week's expiry and buying 750 July 460 puts at 10p and selling 750 July 550 calls at 18p making a credit of 18p for this new position.
If the share price of the tobacco and insurance group falls below 460p, the puts can be exercised to limit further losses from the shareholding.
And if the share price rises, gains will come from the shareholding, but above 550p there is s risk of being assigned the short calls and having to sell the shares at 550p.
Also in BAT options, there was a two-for-one crossed trade in puts which concerned a total of 1,600 July 460 puts at 10p and 800 July 500 puts at 24p changing hands.
By 1540 GMT, BAT shares were down 10p to 506-1/2p.

Elsewhere, in mobile phone company Orange there was a buyer of 750 June 220 calls at 7-1/2p as well as a seller of 500 June 200 puts at 6p. A further 425 puts were sold in the same series also at 6p and in a separate trade.
Shares in Orange were up 2p to 208p.
The main deal in British Petroleum was the sale of 1,000 April 700 calls at 5p ahead of next Wednesday's expiry. BP shares added a penny to 694-1/2p.

Over in the FTSE 100 index options, volatility trades formed the bulk of dealings and one such deal was the sale of 1,000 December 4225 calls at 285-1/2p in Euro-FTSE against buying June FTSE futures at 4298.
By 1530 GMT, spot FTSE was up 12.6 at 4304.9 and June futures were up 12 at 4315.
